quests.instruction: 'Please ___ at the board,' said the teacher, and everyone turned their heads toward it.
quests.hint: The teacher asks everyone to point their eyes in one direction.
quests.explanation: Look means to turn your eyes toward something. Watch is to look at something for a longer time while it moves or changes.
quests.funFact: 'Look' is the one you use when you give someone an instruction to turn their eyes.

quests.instruction: The family sits together on the sofa to ___ a film for two hours.
quests.hint: The thing they are viewing keeps moving and changing.
quests.explanation: Watch means to look at something that moves or changes for some time, like a film, a match or a pot on the stove.
quests.funFact: You watch television, but you look at a picture.

quests.instruction: Ravi was not trying to find anyone, but he suddenly ___ his friend across the street.
quests.hint: It happened without effort or planning.
quests.explanation: See means to notice something with your eyes, often without trying. Look and watch mean you are paying attention on purpose.
quests.funFact: In 'I see!', see means 'I understand'.

quests.instruction: It was raining so loudly that Mia could ___ it all night, even though she did not want to.
quests.hint: The sound reached her ears without any effort.
quests.explanation: Hear means to notice a sound with your ears, even if you do not try. Listen means to pay attention on purpose.
quests.funFact: Hearing is something your ears do all the time, even while you sleep.

quests.instruction: Nina put her phone down and began to ___ carefully to the story her grandmother was telling.
quests.hint: She is giving her full attention.
quests.explanation: Listen means to pay attention to a sound or to someone speaking. You listen on purpose.
quests.funFact: The expression 'listen up' means 'pay attention'.

quests.instruction: Tom was so busy reading that he did not ___ his name being called.
quests.hint: The sound was there, but his mind was somewhere else.
quests.explanation: Hear means that sounds reach your ears. Tom did not even notice the sound.
quests.funFact: You can hear a sound without listening, but you cannot listen without trying to hear.

quests.instruction: '___ me what happened,' Dad said to Leo, who was looking worried.
quests.hint: The word needs a person right after it: me.
quests.explanation: Tell is used with a person: tell me, tell her, tell the teacher. Say goes with the actual words.
quests.funFact: 'Tell me about your day' is a common way for parents to start a conversation.

quests.instruction: Aisha can ___ English, Hindi and a little Spanish.
quests.hint: This verb goes with languages.
quests.explanation: Speak is used when you talk about languages or about making sounds with your voice. 'Say' and 'tell' do not usually go with a language.
quests.funFact: The most commonly spoken first language in the world is Mandarin Chinese.

quests.instruction: The two friends sat under the tree for an hour, ___ about their holiday plans.
quests.hint: It is a conversation between two people.
quests.explanation: Talk means to have a conversation, or to speak with someone. You talk to or with someone about something.
quests.funFact: The word 'talk' can also mean a short speech: He gave a talk about whales.

quests.instruction: Hana's brother is going to the shop, and she asks him to ___ her a loaf of bread when he comes back.
quests.hint: Where is Hana waiting for the bread?
quests.explanation: Bring means to carry something toward the person or place where the speaker will be. Here, Hana will be home.
quests.funFact: 'Bring' moves toward the listener, and 'take' moves away from the speaker.

quests.instruction: Dad is leaving for the office and says, 'I will ___ this report to the manager.'
quests.hint: The report is going away from the place where Dad is speaking.
quests.explanation: Take means to carry something away from where you are. Dad is at home, and the manager is somewhere else.
quests.funFact: 'Take' is often followed by 'to': take it to school.

quests.instruction: At the party, Priya asks her friend, 'Can you ___ your football tomorrow, so we can play here?'
quests.hint: The football will come to the place where Priya will be.
quests.explanation: Bring means to carry something to the place where the speaker is or will be.
quests.funFact: If someone says 'Bring a pencil', it means they will be at the place.

quests.instruction: Sam's pencil case is at home, so he asks Ben if he can ___ a pencil until the end of the lesson.
quests.hint: He will use it for a short time and give it back.
quests.explanation: Borrow means to get something from someone and use it for a short time. You must give it back.
quests.funFact: In a library, you borrow books for free.

quests.instruction: Ben has two pencils, so he is willing to ___ one to Sam for the lesson.
quests.hint: He lets someone use it, and he wants it back.
quests.explanation: Lend means to let someone use something that belongs to you and get it back later.
quests.funFact: 'Lend' and 'borrow' describe the same event from two sides.

quests.instruction: 'Can I ___ you some of my crayons?' Nina asked. 'You can give them back after the lesson.' Which verb fits?
quests.hint: She is the owner who is letting someone use them.
quests.explanation: Lend is what the owner does. The one who gets it for a short time borrows it.
quests.funFact: If you lend a friend a book, you hope to read it again.

quests.instruction: Mum wrote a note on the fridge because she did not want to ___ the dentist appointment.
quests.hint: She wants to avoid a mistake.
quests.explanation: Forget means to not remember something. A note on the fridge helps you not forget.
quests.funFact: Notes help many people avoid forgetting small, important things.

quests.instruction: 'Please ___ me to bring my swimming kit tomorrow,' said Zoe. 'I always forget it.'
quests.hint: She wants someone else to help her think of it.
quests.explanation: Remind means to help someone remember something. You remember it yourself, but someone reminds you.
quests.funFact: A reminder on a phone does the same job as a friend who says, 'Don't forget!'

quests.instruction: Dev tried hard to ___ where he left his jacket and finally thought of the school bus.
quests.hint: It is something he must bring to mind himself.
quests.explanation: Remember means to bring back something from your memory. Dev is doing it by himself.
quests.funFact: Memory works best when you connect new things to things you already know.

quests.instruction: Kofi has lost his key and spends ten minutes ___ it in his bag, without success.
quests.hint: The action is a search that is still going.
quests.explanation: Look for means to search. Find means you succeed in getting something that you were searching for.
quests.funFact: You look for something until you find it.

quests.instruction: After searching in every drawer, Anu finally ___ her missing sock under the bed.
quests.hint: The search is over, and she has the sock.
quests.explanation: Find means to discover something after searching or by chance. It is the result of looking for something.
quests.funFact: The past of 'find' is 'found', and it sounds different from the past of 'fond'.

quests.instruction: Dad's arms are full of grocery bags, so he asks Max to ___ the door open for him.
quests.hint: It means to keep it open in one place.
quests.explanation: Hold means to keep something in one position. You hold a door open, but you carry a bag from place to place.
quests.funFact: If you carry something, you move it; if you hold something, you keep it still.

quests.instruction: The little boy cannot walk far, so his father has to ___ him all the way home.
quests.hint: The boy has to go from one place to another.
quests.explanation: Carry means to hold something or someone and move to another place. Hold alone does not mean moving.
quests.funFact: A baby carrier lets a parent carry a baby close to their body.

quests.instruction: Hana's grandfather ___ glasses all day, because he cannot see well without them.
quests.hint: It describes a state that lasts the whole day, not a single moment.
quests.explanation: Wear describes the state of having clothes on your body. Put on is the action of getting dressed.
quests.funFact: You wear glasses, a watch and a smile.

quests.instruction: It is time to leave, so Hana quickly begins to ___ her shoes by the door.
quests.hint: It is a quick action that starts before she goes out.
quests.explanation: Put on is the action of placing clothes on your body. Wear is the state of already having them on.
quests.funFact: The opposite of 'put on' is 'take off'.

quests.instruction: At the end of the day, Leo is tired and wants to ___ his school uniform.
quests.hint: He is going from dressed to undressed.
quests.explanation: Take off means to remove clothes from your body. It is the opposite of put on.
quests.funFact: 'Take off' is also what a plane does when it leaves the ground.

quests.instruction: Ravi's grandfather ___ him how to play chess last summer.
quests.hint: He is the expert; Ravi is the beginner.
quests.explanation: Teach means to help someone learn something. The teacher teaches, and the student learns.
quests.funFact: The past of 'teach' is 'taught', which sounds like 'tort'.

quests.instruction: Over the summer, Ravi ___ how to play chess from his grandfather.
quests.hint: Ravi gets the knowledge.
quests.explanation: Learn means to get knowledge or a skill. You learn from someone who teaches.
quests.funFact: Learning to play a game is easier when you play with someone who is more skilled.

quests.instruction: Dev's little sister cannot tie her shoelaces yet, so he wants to ___ her.
quests.hint: He is the one who already knows how.
quests.explanation: Teach is followed by the person who gets the knowledge: teach her, teach the class.
quests.funFact: In English, 'teach' and 'learn' are often mixed up, even by adults.

quests.instruction: Nobody told Tom the way, but he ___ it out by himself using the map.
quests.hint: He used his brain to find the answer.
quests.explanation: Work out means to find the answer or solution by thinking about it.
quests.funFact: 'Work out' can also mean to exercise: She works out every morning.

quests.instruction: Sofia says, 'I could not ___ the film; the screen was too far away.' She wanted to make out the small details.
quests.hint: The problem is about her eyes, not her ears.
quests.explanation: See also means to be able to make out something with your eyes. Here it is about being able to view the film.
quests.funFact: The word 'see' can also mean 'meet', as in 'See you tomorrow!'
